P.text: GTELaunchpadV2PairFactory.createPair uses a CREATE2 salt that includes launchpadLp and launchpadFeeDistributor, while Launchpad's pairFor() uses the old salt of just keccak256(token0, token1)
P.evidence_quote: `GTELaunchpadV2PairFactory.createPair` uses a different CREATE2 salt (including `launchpadLp` and `launchpadFeeDistributor`) when CREATE2ing a pair. The `pairFor()` function (used by `Launchpad` to calculate the pair address) still uses the old salt (just `keccak256(token0, token1)`).

I.text: The pair address calculated by Launchpad via pairFor() should match the actual pair address created by the Factory
I.evidence_quote: This asynchronous behavior causes the pair address calculated by `Launchpad` to differ from the actual pair address created by the Factory

V.text: The calculated pair address differs from the actual created pair address, causing transactions referring to the wrong address to fail or assign tokens to an address without code, resulting in lost/stuck tokens and reverts on pair calls
V.evidence_quote: causing transactions referring to the wrong address to fail or assign tokens to an address that does not contain the code (tokens lost)
